math-slq-q1:fc.answer: $Grade (\%) = rise/run \times 100$, where $rise/run = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. Rise and run must be in the same units — convert stations to feet first (station 3+00 = 300 ft) (p. 36)

math-slq-q2:fc.answer: $m_1 = -\frac{1}{m_2}$ — flip the fraction AND negate. Applied to m = 2/3: the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{3}{2}$ (p. 36)

math-log-q3:fc.answer: $\log(xy) = \log x + \log y$ and $\log(x/y) = \log x - \log y$ — combine into one log first (subtraction divides, addition multiplies), then evaluate: $\log_2(64) = 6$ (pp. 36-37)

math-ic-q1:fc.answer: $\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ — for $\int 3x^2\,dx$, raise the power and divide: $3 \cdot \frac{x^3}{3} = x^3$ (p. 50)

math-cc-ex3:fc.answer: $\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1$ — the larger denominator marks the major axis; the full length is $2a$, twice the square root of that denominator (p. 24)

math-log-cp1:fc.answer: $\log_b\!\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_b x - \log_b y$ (quotient rule), then evaluate: $\log_2(48/3) = \log_2(16) = 4$ since $2^4 = 16$ (p. 36)

math-rtt-cp2:fc.answer: $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$ — the 9 m leg is opposite, the 12 m leg adjacent; use inverse tangent: $\theta = \tan^{-1}(9/12) = 36.9°$ (p. 23)

stat-ci-q2:fc.answer: $\bar{x} \pm t_{\alpha/2,\,n-1}\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$ — you only have $s$, not $\sigma$, and with small $n$ the z-interval is too narrow, so use t with $n-1$ degrees of freedom (p. 74)

stat-fri-q1:fc.answer: On a flat surface the normal force equals the weight: $N = W$. Maximum static friction: $F \leq \mu_s N$ (p. 96, Friction)

dyn-wep-q1:fc.answer: $T_1 + V_1 = T_2 + V_2$ — conservation of energy. Mass cancels: $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ regardless of mass (p. 106)

dyn-im-q1:fc.answer: Conservation of momentum with the cars stuck together: $m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = (m_1 + m_2)v'$ — the combined mass is $m_1 + m_2$ (p. 108)

dyn-vib-q3:fc.answer: $\omega_n = \sqrt{k_t / I}$ — torsional stiffness $k_t$ replaces $k$, and mass moment of inertia $I$ replaces $m$ (p. 113)

dyn-wep-ex1:fc.answer: $T_1 + V_1 = T_2 + V_2$ — set $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$; mass cancels, leaving $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ (p. 106)

dyn-wep-ex4:fc.answer: At max compression the block is momentarily at rest ($v = 0$); all kinetic energy is stored in the spring: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$, with $V_e = \frac{1}{2}ks^2$ (p. 106)

dyn-im-cp2:fc.answer: $m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = m_1 v_1' + m_2 v_2'$ — conservation of momentum. Starting from rest, the initial total momentum is zero, so the skater's momentum must balance the ball's (p. 108)

mm-asd-q1:fc.answer: $\sigma = \frac{P}{A}$ — with circular area $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}$, not $\pi d^2$ or $\pi d$ (p. 130)

mom-tsp-q1:fc.answer: $n = E_1/E_2$ — the stiffer material goes in the numerator: $n = E_{steel}/E_{concrete}$ (p. 136)

mom-tsp-q2:fc.answer: $M_p = F_y Z$ — uses the plastic section modulus $Z$, not the elastic $S$ (p. 281)

mom-smd-ex1:fc.answer: $M_{max} = PL$ at the fixed support — moment is zero at the free end and grows linearly to $PL$ at the wall (p. 140)

mom-smd-ex2:fc.answer: $V_{max} = \frac{wL}{2}$ — at the supports, where the shear equals the reaction (p. 140)

mom-smd-cp1:fc.answer: $M_{max} = \frac{wL^2}{2}$ (cantilever, full UDL) at the fixed support — not the simply supported $\frac{wL^2}{8}$, which is a wrong-support-condition trap (p. 140)

mom-cb-cp2:fc.prompt: Radius of gyration: what is the formula in terms of I and A?

mom-tsp-cp1:fc.prompt: Shape factor: what is the formula, and what does it measure?
mom-tsp-cp1:fc.answer: $SF = Z/S$ — the reserve strength between first yield and the full plastic moment (p. 281)

mat-wm-q1:fc.prompt: MC = (W_wet − W_OD)/W_OD × 100 — what weight goes in the denominator?
mat-wm-q1:fc.answer: $MC = (W_{wet} - W_{OD})/W_{OD} \times 100$ — the denominator is the oven-dry weight $W_{OD}$, not the wet weight

fm-fp-q1:fc.answer: $SG = \frac{\gamma}{\gamma_w}$, so $\gamma = SG \times \gamma_w$ — with water reference $\gamma_w = 9{,}810\ \text{N/m}^3$ in SI (p. 176)

fm-hp-q1:fc.answer: $P_2 - P_1 = -\gamma(z_2 - z_1) = \gamma h$ gives Pa — divide by 1,000 for kPa (49,050 Pa = 49.05 kPa); reporting 49,050 kPa means the Pa-to-kPa conversion was skipped (p. 177)

fm-cb-q1:fc.answer: $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$ — with $A = \pi D^2/4$ the $\pi/4$ cancels, so $v_2 = v_1(D_1/D_2)^2$: exponent 2, because area scales with $D^2$ (p. 180)

fm-das-q2:fc.answer: $Fr_m = Fr_p \Rightarrow \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{g l_m}} = \frac{v_p}{\sqrt{g l_p}}$ — g cancels, so $v \propto \sqrt{L}$: the exponent is 1/2 because Fr contains $\sqrt{gl}$ (p. 196)

flu-fp-ex1:fc.answer: $\gamma = \rho g$ — density times gravitational acceleration; the product is force per volume, $\text{N/m}^3$ (p. 176)

flu-fp-ex3:fc.answer:

u =  rac{\mu}{ho}$, so $\mu = 
uho$ — $
u$ is kinematic viscosity, $\mu$ is dynamic (absolute) viscosity (p. 176)

flu-hfb-ex1:fc.answer: $F_R = \gamma h_C A$ — circular gate area $A = \pi D^2/4$; $h_C$ is the depth of the gate's centroid below the surface, 4 m here (p. 179)

flu-pfh-ex1:fc.prompt: For laminar flow (Re < 2,100), what is the friction factor formula?

flu-fm-ex1:fc.answer: $v = \sqrt{\frac{2(P_0 - P_s)}{\rho}}$ — $\Delta P$ is stagnation pressure minus static pressure, and it must be in Pa to pair with $\rho$ in $\text{kg/m}^3$ (p. 194)

surv-hc-q2:fc.prompt: What is the horizontal curve tangent distance formula?

surv-ac-ex2:fc.answer: $A = w\left(\frac{h_1 + h_n}{2} + h_2 + h_3 + \cdots + h_{n-1}\right)$ — the first and last offsets are averaged (halved); all interior offsets count at full value (p. 280)

surv-lev-cp1:fc.answer: Backsights are added, foresights subtracted: $\text{Elev}_{\text{final}} = \text{Elev}_{\text{start}} + \Sigma BS - \Sigma FS$ (p. 309)

wr-wq-ex1:fc.answer: $BOD_t = L_0(1 - e^{-kt})$ — the exponent is $-kt = -0.23 \times 3 = -0.69$; $e^{-kt}$ is the fraction of ultimate BOD not yet exerted at time t (p. 321)

str-ds-q1:fc.answer: $m + r = 2j$: stable and determinate. If $m + r > 2j$: indeterminate (needs compatibility equations); if $m + r < 2j$: unstable mechanism (p. 271)

str-ds-q2:fc.answer: Compare $3m + r$ to $3j + c$ — a pin support provides 2 reaction components, a fixed support provides 3 (p. 271)

str-dvw-q3:fc.prompt: End-loaded cantilever: what is the tip deflection formula?

str-ind-q2:fc.answer: $R = \frac{3wL}{8}$ at the prop — less than $wL/2$ because the fixed end carries the larger share of the load

str-ind-q3:fc.answer: $M_{FE} = \frac{wL^2}{12}$ — smaller than $\frac{wL^2}{8}$, which is the simple-span midspan moment, not a fixed-end moment

str-il-q2:fc.answer: Peak ordinate $= L/4$ at midspan; place the load directly at midspan for max moment: $M_{max} = P \times L/4$ (p. 268)

str-rcc-q2:fc.prompt: ACI column reinforcement ratio: what are the minimum and maximum ρ_g limits?

str-st-q1:fc.answer: $P_n = F_y A_g$ with $\phi_y = 0.90$ — yielding uses the gross area $A_g$, no bolt-hole deductions (p. 283)

str-st-q2:fc.answer: $A_n = \left[b_g - \Sigma\left(d_b + \tfrac{1}{8}\text{ in.}\right)\right] t$ — subtract $d_b + 1/8$ in. per hole; the extra 1/8 in. is 1/16 in. hole clearance plus 1/16 in. drilling damage (p. 282)

str-il-ex1:fc.answer: $\eta_{R_A}(x) = \frac{L - x}{L}$ — the right reaction uses $x/L$ instead (p. 268)

str-rfs-ex1:fc.answer: $a = \frac{A_s f_y}{0.85 f_c' b}$ — the 0.85 on $f_c'$ in the denominator is the factor students most often forget (p. 275)

str-sb-ex3:fc.answer: $V_n = 0.6 F_y A_w C_{v1}$ — uses the web area $A_w = d \times t_w$, not the full section area; the shear yield coefficient is 0.6 (p. 281)

str-sc-ex1:fc.answer: $\frac{KL}{r}$ — convert $KL$ from feet to inches before dividing, because $r$ is in inches; skipping the conversion gives 6.7 instead of 80 (p. 281)

str-st-ex1:fc.answer: $A_n = \left[b_g - \Sigma\left(d_b + \tfrac{1}{8}\text{ in.}\right)\right] t$ — deduct $(d_b + 1/8\text{ in.})$ for every hole at the cross-section: two here (p. 282)

str-ind-ex1:fc.answer: Each fixed end provides 3 reaction components (H, V, M), so $r = 6$; $DSI = r - 3 = 3$

str-ds-cp1:fc.answer: Each fixed support contributes 3 reaction components; use $\text{Degree} = (3m + r) - (3j + c)$ (p. 271)

str-sb-cp2:fc.answer: $V_n = 0.6 F_y A_w C_{v1}$ — the web area $A_w = d \times t_w$ resists shear; 0.6 relates shear yield stress to $F_y$ (p. 281)

str-st-cp2:fc.answer: $A_e = U A_n$, $U = 1 - \frac{\bar{x}}{L}$ — $\bar{x}$ is the distance from the connection plane to the member centroid, $L$ is the connection length (p. 282)

geo-sc-q1:fc.answer: $\text{A-line: } PI = 0.73(LL - 20)$ — plotting above the A-line means clay (C); silts (M) plot below (p. 267)

geo-sc-q2:fc.answer: $C_u = \frac{D_{60}}{D_{10}} \geq 6$ and $C_c = \frac{(D_{30})^2}{D_{10} \times D_{60}}$ between 1 and 3 — here $C_c = 0.83$ fails the 1-3 range, so the sand is SP (p. 267)

geo-sc-q3:fc.answer: $\text{A-line: } PI = 0.73(LL - 20) = 0.73(35) = 25.6$ — the actual PI = 28 plots above the A-line, meaning clay: CH since LL > 50 (p. 267)

geo-co-q2:fc.answer: $T_v = \frac{c_v \cdot t}{H_{dr}^2}$ — two-way drainage means $H_{dr} = H/2$; since $t \propto H_{dr}^2$, two-way drainage consolidates four times faster than one-way (p. 262)

geo-ss-q1:fc.answer: $\tau_f = c + \sigma_N \tan \phi$ — cohesion $c$ plus the frictional component: normal stress $\sigma_N$ times the tangent of friction angle $\phi$ (p. 263)

geo-ss-q2:fc.prompt: For c=0, what is the formula for sinφ from a triaxial test?

geo-seep-q2:fc.answer: $i_c = (G_s - 1)/(1 + e)$ — the gradient at which a quick condition occurs in saturated sand (p. 260)

geo-le-q2:fc.answer: The pressure diagram is a triangle; the resultant is $P_a = \frac{1}{2} K_a \gamma H^2$ (p. 263)

geo-rw-q1:fc.answer: $FS_{\text{overturning}} = \frac{\Sigma M_R}{M_O}$ — the resisting moments $\Sigma M_R$ go in the numerator (p. 264)

geo-bc-ex1:fc.answer: $q_u = cN_c + qN_q + \frac{1}{2}\gamma B N_\gamma$ — with $\phi = 0$, $N_\gamma = 0$, so only $cN_c$ and $qN_q$ survive; $q = \gamma D_f$, the overburden at footing depth (p. 264)

geo-le-cp1:fc.answer: An unyielding (rigid) wall is the at-rest case — use $K_0 = 1 - \sin \phi$, then $P_0 = \frac{1}{2} K_0 \gamma H^2$ (p. 263)

geo-rw-cp2:fc.answer: $q_{min} = \frac{\Sigma V}{B}\left(1 - \frac{6e}{B}\right)$ — valid when $e \leq B/6$ (resultant inside the middle third, full base in compression) (p. 264)

trans-st-q1:fc.answer: $y = t + \frac{v}{2a \pm 64.4G}$ — $v$ must be in ft/sec: multiply mph by 1.467 (p. 300)

trans-cl-q1:fc.prompt: What is the heavy-vehicle adjustment factor formula?

trans-ssd-ex1:fc.answer: Braking only: $\frac{V^2}{30\left(\frac{a}{32.2} \pm G\right)}$ — the denominator is 30 times the deceleration ratio $a/32.2$ adjusted by grade; drop the $1.47Vt$ reaction term (p. 300)

trans-vc-ex1:fc.answer: $K = \frac{L}{A}$ — $A$ is the algebraic grade difference in percent ($A = |g_2 - g_1| \times 100$), so K comes out in ft per percent change (p. 301)

const-ev-q1:fc.answer: $CV = BCWP - ACWP$ — earned value (BCWP) minus actual cost (ACWP); negative means over budget (p. 310)

const-pf-q1:fc.answer: $CPI = \frac{BCWP}{ACWP}$ — earned value over actual cost; CPI < 1.0 means over budget (p. 311)
